sources.entry: napkin-to-blueprint by Tapas Mukherjee - A five-stage pipeline of Claude Code slash commands and specialized subagents that turns a raw product idea into a build-ready blueprint: an interview-driven brief, researched feature definitions, per-feature specs with acceptance criteria, and an architecture with a database schema.

summary.one_liner: n2b (Napkin to Blueprint) is a five-stage pipeline of slash commands and subagents that runs inside Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or Cursor and turns a raw product idea into a build-ready product blueprint, without writing application code.
summary.what_it_does: Stage 1 interviews the user about the idea and writes a structured project brief, reading any existing notes first. Stage 2 uses researcher, visionary, and synthesizer agents to produce a seven-document product definition (market research, personas, journeys, prioritized feature list, scope, success metrics, assumptions), checked by a completeness audit. Stage 3 writes per-feature specs with verbatim acceptance criteria, run in batches with checkpoints, plus a dependency map and reconciliation log. Stage 4 produces a feasibility analysis, a recommended architecture with documented alternatives, and a database schema. Stage 5 optionally exports the blueprint for targets such as a dev brief, Jira CSV, backlog JSON/CSV, agent workspace, GitHub Spec Kit, PRD for Task Master/BMAD, or prompt packs for Lovable, v0, Bolt, and Replit. An installer (npx) places the commands into the chosen runtime's directory, and a /n2b:status command reports progress and next steps.
use_cases: turn a raw app idea into a product spec before coding
generate feature specs with acceptance criteria
create a PRD or architecture doc from an idea
prepare a handoff package for a dev team or coding agent
write a Jira backlog from a product idea
produce prompts for vibe-coding tools like Lovable or Bolt
how_to_run: Restart the runtime, then run /n2b:s1-init (Claude Code form)
stack: Markdown commands, workflows, and agent definitions
JSON model catalog and config templates
Claude Code, Codex CLI (>= 0.130.0), OpenCode, or Cursor as host runtime
notable: Runs inside existing AI coding agents across four runtimes, with translated command formats per host
Deliberately stops at the blueprint and does not build the product
Stage 5 exports to many targets, including Spec Kit, Jira, PRD, and vibe-coding prompt packs, each checked by a fidelity gate
Smoke mode (--smoke) caps Stage 2 features so the full pipeline can be rehearsed quickly
Model tier profiles route 16 agent roles to different models per provider
caveats: Requires an AI coding runtime (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or Cursor); Codex needs CLI 0.130.0 or later and may need a folder rename for skills
Stage 3 runs in multiple batches and needs several command invocations, consuming provider quota
Does not write application code, scaffold projects, or set up databases; output is an input to a build
keywords: plan a new app before coding
turn my app idea into a plan
write user stories from an idea
market research for a product idea
